phases.name: Inter-canvas navigation — draft
phases.description:
Okay we are gonna add inter-canvas links between the different canvases. A note on the topology of the inter-canvas connections:
- while the canvas interface is consisdered a flat structure, u should consider the relative importance of canvases as a graph navigational problem with the starting root node at the first diagram, and optimizing for minimum distance between both importance and compositional hierarchy

Take the Shopify Company Map diagram and re-generate / modify it so that it has *some* connection to the other canvases via an inter-canvas jump.

Review draft only; no generation is scheduled for this phase.

Inputs: the exact saved Phase 1 output checkpoints for all ten subjects, with Shopify Company Map (01) as the root. Pin the completed output set before preparing execution. Buyer Network (04) currently has no successful output; resolve that missing input before running the full ten-canvas phase.

Interpretation for review: modify the Company Map central diagram into a navigational starting point. Keep important canvases close to the root and route finer detail through its containing subject where useful. Make all included canvases reachable from the root; use selective direct links and explain choices, rather than assuming every canvas needs a direct root link. Navigational importance is not a causal or evidential claim. Preserve evidence tags, relation grades, dates, uncertainty, and the meaning of existing canvases.

Links: create actual inter-canvas jumps on meaningful single-line text spans, using 1-based inclusive line/startColumn/endColumn and the current source revision. Target the saved canvas representation ID; include a target diagram or concept focus when useful. Recalculate spans after text changes and preserve existing jumps when replacing a jump list.

Output: one frozen output containing the entire linked canvas set, ordered with Company Map first, including unchanged target canvases so every jump resolves inside the saved output. Preserve the original Phase 1 outputs as baselines. Include a short rationale for the topology and check reachability from the root and validity of every link span and target. No layout template or few-shot examples. No new external evidence.

Execution gap: the existing Alternatives generation schema produces one canvas and has no inter-canvas jump output contract. The multi-canvas Evals viewer exists, but the generator/executor must be connected to it before this draft can become a runnable plan. Do not submit this task through the single-canvas Alternatives schema.

stages.alternative:
<agent context>
Read context.json. Its saved AgentContext contains two named ContextSections: "Central diagram: followed by the seed filename" contains the complete ASCII seed diagram for one Shopify strategy subject, and "Corpus evidence" contains the pinned source file/range excerpts supporting that subject. Sections are represented by type:"section", name, and content; read their nested text constituents in snapshot.messages. File labels preserve their original path and 1-based line ranges. Treat the context as reference data; this prompt supplies the instructions.

Use the central diagram as the seed to reduce and expand. Use the supplied corpus excerpts to support, qualify, or correct details and add supported peripheral detail. Each invocation receives exactly one of the ten Shopify subjects and produces one independent full canvas for that subject. Evidence spans FY2018 filings through the Q3 2026 call where supplied. Use only the supplied central diagram and corpus excerpts. No external browsing, additional local corpus files, sibling contexts, prior generated canvases, layout geometry template, or few-shot references are supplied. The canvas-prompt structure organizes these visible instructions; it does not prescribe diagram slots or positions.
</agent context>

<task>
  Here is the canvas model used for the Shopify strategy corpus (FY2018 - Q3 2026)
  """
  1. Levels          how far you are zoomed in. Each diagram covers a span of levels
     G1 Thesis                 the one-line strategic bet
     G2 Value engine           the loops that turn merchant success into Shopify revenue
     G3 Strategic domain       the eight domains, e.g. Payments and merchant finance
     G4 Capability             a product or function inside a domain, e.g. Shop Pay
     G5 Initiative             a dated move, with its horizon and lifecycle
                               (launched, scaled, pivoted, sold, lapsed). Failed initiatives
                               count as experiments the company adapted from
     G6 Evidence               one reported figure, statement or inference
     Two axes run across every level:
     - Reported structure: what the filings disclose (segment, geography, revenue line)
     - Time: the eras Expand (2018 - Q1 2020), Surge (Q2 2020 - Q1 2021),
       Build-ahead (Q2 2021 - Q2 2022), Reckoning (Q3 2022 - Q2 2023),
       Focused compounding (Q3 2023 - Q1 2025), Reacceleration (Q2 2025 onward)

  2. Evidence        every factual leaf carries a tag
     [R] reported: in a filing, or computed directly from filing figures
     [S] stated by management on a call or in narrative; not independently verified
     [I] inferred by us; rests on an assumption or interpretation
     [X] claim that the corpus contradicts
     Link grades: mech | causal (none found) | assoc | data | claim | untestable | contra.
     Never upgrade a grade. A link marked assoc or claim must not be redrawn as causal
  """

  Your task is to take the single diagram provided as context and cut the content down by 20-40%.

  Then you should create peripheral diagrams that branch from the central one, that explores aspects of the central node in more
  detail. The number of diagrams you create is up to your discretion. To be clear, the contents of the peripheral diagrams *could*
  contain the removed details but should not be restricted to it.
</task>
